Account.description:
Someone with their email, as they see themself and as the organisers
of a contest they registered for see them.
Account.title: Account

CallbackAnswer.description: Where the grading stands once its run's report is taken.
CallbackAnswer.title: CallbackAnswer

Change.description:
One entry of a place's history: the version it made, who made it, what
they said about it and when.
Change.title: Change

Closed.description: Why a task is not open, the first of these that applies.
Closed.title: Closed

ContestHome.description:
A contest's home for the caller. `organises` says the caller holds a
role at the contest, which keeps them from registering;
`registration_open` says whether the registration window is open now,
`invite_only` whether only invited people may register and `asks_code`
whether registering takes the contest's code. `deadline` is the
contest's end plus the caller's own extension.
ContestHome.title: ContestHome

ContestNames.description: A contest by the names of its org and itself.
ContestNames.title: ContestNames

ContestSummary.description:
A contest the caller sees, with its title, when it runs, who sees it,
and the caller's own registration status.
ContestSummary.title: ContestSummary

ContestVisibility.description:
Who sees the contest: visitors and everyone signed in, anyone with a
session, or only its contestants and organisers.
ContestVisibility.title: ContestVisibility

Contestant.description:
One registration as the contest's organisers read it: the same
fields, and who the person is, null once their account is gone.
Contestant.title: Contestant

ContestantInput.description:
One input the contestant gives, with what its form shows: `label`,
the `language` choices of a code input, `min` and `max` of a number,
the `accept` patterns and `max_size` in bytes of a file, and a
`default`. The submit panel shows one field or drop zone per input, and
an input with no label by its id.
ContestantInput.title: ContestantInput

CreateContest.description: A contest to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateContest.title: CreateContest

CreateTask.description: A task to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateTask.title: CreateTask

CreateWorkflow.description:
A workflow to make under `owner`: the caller's own username, or the
name of an org where they hold the manager role or above.
CreateWorkflow.title: CreateWorkflow

DefinitionError.description:
One thing wrong with a definition file: its YAML path, "" for the file
as a whole, and a sentence a form shows beside that field.
DefinitionError.title: DefinitionError

Draft.description:
A save kept as a draft: the version its files were written as, the
errors that kept it from publishing, and what it held back.
Draft.title: Draft

ExtensionRequest.description:
How long past the contest's end this person may still submit, in
seconds, in place of any extension they had.
ExtensionRequest.title: ExtensionRequest

FileChange.description:
One file of a save, with the token it was read with, or null for a
file the save creates.
FileChange.title: FileChange

FileContent.description: One file at one version, with the token a write presents back.
FileContent.title: FileContent

ForgeUrl.description:
Where a browser reaches the forge's own pages: sign-in and the account
settings. No trailing slash.
ForgeUrl.title: ForgeUrl

GradedTest.description:
One test's row of a verdict: its name as the task spells it, its own
outcome, its time in milliseconds and peak memory in KiB, each null when
the step was not measured, its named numbers, and the checker's note
when there is one.
GradedTest.title: GradedTest

Grading.description:
One grading as an organiser managing its task reads it: the
submission by its number, the publication it grades against, its stage
and attempt, where it stands, the reason it failed, its verdict, whether
its log was written, the last progress its run reported, and its times.
Grading.title: Grading

GradingProgress.description:
The last progress a grading's run reported: the step it was at and how
many of that step's containers were done of how many.
GradingProgress.title: GradingProgress

GradingStatus.description:
Where one grading stands. `queued` waits for its run to be started,
which happens as soon as the request that made it commits; `dispatched`
is held by the CI, waiting for a machine or checking out; `running` has
had its envelope fetched by the harness. It ends `done` with a verdict,
`cancelled` by an organiser, or `system_error`, a grading that failed for
a reason of the platform's, never a grade: its run could not be started,
or did not report before its deadline.
GradingStatus.title: GradingStatus

GrantRequest.description:
Give the named user `role` at the scope, moving them from any other
role they hold directly there.
GrantRequest.title: GrantRequest

HeldRole.description: A role the user holds, at the org, contest or task `names` reaches.
HeldRole.title: HeldRole

Holder.description:
Someone holding `role` at the scope asked about, held directly at
`at_names`: that scope, or a broader one, such as the org of a contest
whose admin is listed at the contest.
Holder.title: Holder

InputType.description:
The type of one input, the same on the contestant's side and the
setter's (TASK-FORMAT.md section 2).
InputType.title: InputType

Limits.description:
What a submit is checked against: how many submissions in all, how
often, and how large, in bytes.
Limits.title: Limits

Me.description:
The signed-in user and their roles at every scope. `degraded` is set
when the forge did not answer and the identity comes from the session.
Me.title: Me

MyRegistration.description:
The caller's own registration: where it stands, when it was made and
last decided, why it was rejected, and how long past the contest's end
they may still submit, in seconds.
MyRegistration.title: MyRegistration

Named.description: An org, a contest or a task, by the name people call it.
Named.title: Named

NotReady.description:
Deliberately not a problem document: an orchestrator reads the status in
a fixed place. What failed underneath is in the log and not here.
NotReady.title: NotReady

Person.description:
Someone as another person sees them, by their forge id. Their email
stays out.
Person.title: Person

Problem.description: Extra members are allowed: `sole_admin` carries `scopes`, for instance.
Problem.title: Problem

PublicContest.description:
A public contest `where` it is, by the names of its org and itself,
with its title as `name`, what it says of itself and when it runs.
`tasks` are its released tasks, and empty in the list of contests.
PublicContest.title: PublicContest

PublicStatement.description: A released task of a public contest with its statement in Markdown.
PublicStatement.title: PublicStatement

PublicTask.description:
A released task of a public contest: its name, the label the contest
gives it, and its title.
PublicTask.title: PublicTask

Publication.description:
One publication: its number among the task's publications, the version
it froze, whether it changed how the task grades and what, and when.
Which workflow each of its workflow names was at the forge stays out.
Publication.title: Publication

Published.description:
A save that published: the new publication's number among the task's,
whether it changed how the task grades, and what.
Published.title: Published

Rate.description: At most `count` submissions in any `per` seconds.
Rate.title: Rate

RegisterRequest.description: The code the contest asks for, when it asks for one.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

RejectRequest.description: Why, in words the person reads on their own page.
RejectRequest.title: RejectRequest

Rejudged.description:
What a rejudge did: the publication the new attempts grade against,
how many it queued, how many unfinished attempts against an older
publication it cancelled first, how many it left to finish against the
current one, and how many it passed over because the current
publication no longer has their stage.
Rejudged.title: Rejudged

Result.description:
One grading of a submission at one stage, as its contestant sees it:
its id, stage, attempt and status, the stage's `show`, and of its
verdict what that allows: the `outcome`, the named `metrics`, the
`summary` and a row for every test. `log` says whether its run log can
be read.
Result.title: Result

RollbackFile.description:
Write the file as it was at `version` back as a new change, `token`
being the one of the file as it is now.
RollbackFile.title: RollbackFile

SaveRequest.description:
The files a save writes, several at once. `keep_as_draft` writes them
as a draft that says what it held back and publishes nothing, on any
save. Otherwise, while the task's contest runs, `confirm` publishes a
change to how the task grades; an empty save with `confirm` publishes a
draft kept earlier.
SaveRequest.title: SaveRequest

ScopeNames.description:
The names of the org, the contest and the task a scope reaches, as far
down as it does, in the shape of an address: `acme`, `acme/spring`,
`acme/spring/sum`.
ScopeNames.title: ScopeNames

SessionInfo.description:
One place this user is signed in, described by its device and its
times. The address a session came from is kept for the record and stays
out of the answer.
SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo

Show.description: What a contestant sees of a stage's result.
Show.title: Show

Slot.description:
A slot for one file: where to send it, and when the slot stops being
good. `ready` is true for a file the forge already holds, which is sent
again by sending nothing.
Slot.title: Slot

Submission.description:
One of the caller's submissions of the task: its number among them,
when it was taken, and its grading at each stage in the order the task
lists its stages.
Submission.title: Submission

SubmitRequest.description:
A submit: `idempotency_key` is 8 to 128 letters, digits, `-` and `_`,
made once by the browser for this submit, so sending it again answers
with the submission it made and makes nothing. `inputs` is keyed by the
id of each of the task's contestant inputs, and forge checks them
against the task's inputs.
SubmitRequest.title: SubmitRequest

SubmittedFileInput.description:
What one input of a submission was: the paths of its files in the
submission, each readable at the file route, and the language of a code
input; or the value given. It is read leniently from the submission's
`submission.json`: a member of the wrong type is left out rather than
failing the answer.
SubmittedFileInput.title: SubmittedFileInput

SubmittedFiles.description:
What a submission was made with, by input id, so a page can put it
back into the upload panel.
SubmittedFiles.title: SubmittedFiles

SubmittedInput.description:
What a contestant gives for one input: the uploads of its files, and
for a code input the language chosen; or, for a text, number or
true-or-false input, its value.
SubmittedInput.title: SubmittedInput

TaskEntry.description:
A task released to the caller: its name, the label and points the
contest gives it, its title, and whether they may submit to it now.
TaskEntry.title: TaskEntry

TaskPage.description:
A task as the caller reads it: its statement in Markdown, the limits
a submit is checked against and the inputs a contestant gives, and
nothing else the task holds.
TaskPage.title: TaskPage

TaskRelease.description:
Whether the task is released, visible and open to one person now, and
when it is not open, the first reason why.
TaskRelease.title: TaskRelease

TaskState.description:
Where a task's files stand: the version at their head, the latest
publication or none, and whether the head is a draft, a state no
publication froze. A draft carries the errors that keep it from
publishing; a draft with none was held back, or has not been saved since
it was made.
TaskState.title: TaskState

UpdateOrg.description: The org's description, and its display name when given.
UpdateOrg.title: UpdateOrg

Upload.description:
Where one upload stands: the input it is for, its name and content
type, the size and digest declared for it, and its status. `verified` is
an upload a submit may name.
Upload.title: Upload

UploadRequest.description:
One file to upload for the task's contestant input `input`: the name
it is committed under, its size in bytes, the SHA-256 of its content in
lowercase hex and, when the browser knows it, its content type.

The digest is what the forge checks the bytes against as they arrive, so
a file that changed between being read and being sent is refused there
rather than committed.
UploadRequest.title: UploadRequest

UploadStatus.description:
Where an upload stands: `waiting` until the forge holds its bytes,
`verified` once the forge says it does, and `consumed` once a commit
holds the pointer to it.
UploadStatus.title: UploadStatus

Verdict.description:
What a run's verdict says of the submission: its outcome, its named
numbers, its summary and a row for every test. Where the run put its log
and the forge's names for what it graded stay out.
Verdict.title: Verdict

Workflow.description: A workflow, by its owner and its name.
Workflow.title: Workflow

WriteFile.description:
One file written, `token` being the one it was read with or null for
a new file. For a task this is a save, and `confirm` and
`keep_as_draft` do what they do for one.
WriteFile.title: WriteFile

Written.description: A contest's file written: the version the change made.
Written.title: Written

`invalid_callback`, and a grading that takes no reports now

fetch, a grading the CI holds no run of, or one whose deadline has
passed, `grading_closed`. It carries the run's callback token, so it is
never stored on the way.
